questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
UBC has an excellent reputation as being one of the top universities in Canada. I wanted to go somewhere with a high academic level.

Furthermore, the university is know for its many social opportunities. UBC has hundreds of social clubs where you can dive into every interest imaginable.

I also love doing outdoor activities, and Vancouver is arguably the best destination in the world for this. With its close proximity to both the ocean and the mountains, Vancouver provides easy acces to activities such as hiking, camping, rock climbing, mountain biking, skiing, kayaking, diving, whale watching etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I had an excellent experience during my exchange. Classes were great, teachers were professional, the other students were open and fun to hang out with and the city and the surrounding area was amazing.

The only reason that I don't rate it 10/10 is because I had to compromise a bit on the courses that I took. I still had some really good courses, but many of the courses that I originally wanted to take, were not available.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. Everyone was really helpful, and a lot of information is already provided via email. They also have an orientation day before the classes start.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: GoGlobal assisted me when I had trouble with my courses. I ended up changing two of my courses during the first two weeks, and the staff were really helpful with finding the right courses for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is lots of housing options available for students in various students residents. I was told that 50 % of applicants receive housing, and I was one of the lucky ones. The apartments are usually shared with 3-5 other students, who each have their own room but share kitchen and bathroom facilities.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Lots of meal plan opportunities, although they are (in my opinion) expensive and not worth it. Instead, the university offers lots of cheap takeaway of various sorts. The apartments also have decent kitchens, but you need to bring your own kitchen utensils.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
You need to bring your own bedsheets, duvet, pillow, kitchen utensils and sometimes wifi router. The walls are also really thin, so privacy can be limited.

However, staying on campus is still one of the best choices I made, since everything is so close by. There is so much to do on campus, and staying in a student residence makes it much easier to get to classes, student clubs, social activites, the library etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would've rated it 5/5 if we didn't have to bring so much stuff ourselves. It is expensive and not very environmentally friendly for new exchange students to buy and throw out so much stuff every semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very long and with many steps, especially with Erasmus.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First, you have to send an application to UCPH. Once it's approved, you also have to apply at UBC. Once that's approved as well, you have to apply for pre approval of courses (regardless of whether you have decided on your courses). You then apply for your courses.

If you receive an Erasmus grant, there are a few extra steps, including filling out an Online Learning Agreement, which has to be signed by the Erasmus responsible at both universities.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A few online guides are available for help as well as email reminders.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded in registering for the classes that I wanted. However, I also found out that not all the classes that are featured on their website are available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just know that it's time consuming. And that you aren't guaranteed to get the classes that you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the classes and teachers were great!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There are 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 level courses, depending on what year you're on. As BA exchange students, we can take anything from 100-400 level courses. There is a noticable difference between the different levels. However, in general, I found the level to be the same as, or easier, than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Like at UCPH, the classes were often divided into lectures and discussions/lab. 

In general, there were more projects to do at UBC, such as assignments and presentations. My classes also included noticably more field work, like learning about plants while walking around the forest.

One difference, that I personally found to be brilliant at UBC, was the fact that the course grade isn't determined by a single exam. Instead, the course grade is based on quizzes, assignments, presentations, midterm exams, final exams etc. that all count a little towards the final grade. This makes it much less stressful and removes a lot of the pressure during exam season.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Introduction to Conservation
2. Forest Ecology
3. Atmospheric Environments
4. Issues in Genomics and the Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My two favorite courses were Forest Ecology and Introduction to Conservation. 

I liked Forest Ecology because it included a lot of field work in the forest. The course also included many interesting and relevant topics, such as climate change, forest management and forest fires.

Introduction to Conservation was especially interesting because it included many different approaches to nature conservation, both historically, politically and scientifically. It gave some new perspectives on this very relevant topic and allowed me to reflect on the state of our world.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
A mandatory health insurance (iMED) at UBC of approx. 1700 dkk. This was on top of my already paid travel insurance of 2800 dkk.

There is also a 250 dkk housing application when applying for on campus housing.

You also have to get used to Canadian taxes. The prices that you see are always before taxes are added, which can be up to 12 % extra.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Take away food was much less expensive than anticipated. On the other hand, groceries were more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was one of my favorite things about UBC!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is an abundance of social clubs to join. Personally, I was in the outdoor club (VOC), diving club (Aqua Society) and chess club. All of which have my highest recommendations.

On top of that, the university offers free access to the aquatic centre as well as free badminton, basketball, table tennis and much more. You can also get a very cheap fitness membership. 

You can also watch hockey/football games for free and participate in various arranged activities throughout the semester, such as the Day of the Longboat, which is a boat race for students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the things mentioned above.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- Banff National Park - it's far away but incredibly beautiful and worth the trip.
- Vancouver Island
- Whistler
- Local mountains
- Local ski resorts
- Downtown Vancouver
- Whale watching
- Hockey games

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is not totally different from European culture, so I found it quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join student clubs, attend events and just be open in general.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In Downtown Vancouver (1 hour from campus), there is a lot of drug addicts and homeless people. Seeing how they live their lives came as a bit of a shock.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Canadians are very open and the environment was very inclusive.

They also put a lot of effort into acknowledging the lands of their indigenous ancestors, which I found interesting.

I liked the fact that UBC and Vancouver in general holds a blend of many different cultures. Only a handful of the people I met were born and raised in the city. There were many people from other parts of Canada, Europe and especially Asia.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You couldn't pick a better destination for exchange. You can do anything here.
2. It's not the cheapest destination. Especially groceries and housing can be a big expense in Vancouver.
3. Make sure to take advantage of all the opportunities that are presented to you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hold back. It's an experience of a lifetime.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the incredible experiences, enjoying the beautiful Canadian nature and meeting amazing people from around the world that I am still in contact with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating between academic responsibilities and social opportunities, as I found it difficult to find the time for alle the social events and travel experiences that I wanted to pursue while also managing my schoolwork. Fortunately, it all worked out just fine in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
